rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=2, train_n=400, n_iter=60, val_n=200, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, lr=0.003, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, img_sr=0.0002, outer_wall_s=900, seed=42, rationale=iter-15 dual_domain_bilateral_n2i, ONE-KNOB: n_iter 30->60 at the NAILED optimal lr=3e-3 (iter-13 champion hr=0.1988; iter-14 lr3.5e-3 was 0.1973 = ridge top confirmed at 3e-3). img_sr=0.0002, kernel=7, spatial=1.5 all fixed at their tested optima. HYPOTHESIS: iter-8 (n_iter 30->100) DROPPED hr, BUT that was at the OVERSHOOTING lr=5e-3 where extra steps drift the fit toward the noisy 64-view half-target. Now at the GENTLE lr=3e-3 the per-scene fit does NOT overshoot, so MORE steps (60) should let the edge-preserving BF converge FURTHER on genuine denoising -> hr climbs above 0.1988. This is the lr x n_iter interaction: gentle-lr + more-steps is the classic well-damped-convergence regime. If hr FLAT/DROPS, 30 steps already converge the 6-param BF (tiny model converges fast) and n_iter is saturated at the optimal lr -> the ~0.199 hr is the edge-preserving N2I ceiling. RISK: 60 steps x 200 scenes may approach outer_wall_s=900 -> possible val_n trim; iter-13 ran 694s at n_iter30 on a fast node, n_iter60 ~1100-1300s could trim a few scenes (noted if so). ONE knob: n_iter 30->60.
